text: Before starting a Duel, you must have a deck(s). There are 3 kinds of decks:
• Main Deck (must contain 40 - 60 cards): This deck contain all of your mainly used cards including [{Monsters|monsters}], [{Spells|spells}], [{Traps|traps}],...
• Extra Deck (must contain 0 - 15 cards): This deck contain monsters that can be only Special Summoned. Those monsters can bring a huge advantage to your tactics.

• Side Deck (must contain 0 - 15 cards): For normal Duel, you don't need a Side Deck, but in standard Match which includes 3 Duels, after finish the first Duel, you will want to alter the contents of the Main Deck and Extra Deck to duel with opponent's deck(s). Therefore, you will need a Side Deck that contain cards which has special uses.
Notice:
Extra Deck and Side Deck are optional, so you can still play without them.
Every card in Extra Deck cannot exist in hand or Main Deck and must be returned to Extra Deck in those cases (except for the special cases, {[card effect can overwrite this rule|66100045]})
After altering your Main Deck / Extra Deck, the number of cards in each decks must remain the same.
A Yu-gi-oh Duel is conducted on a playmat, like the following one:
Deck Zone & Extra Deck Zone: Each players have 2 zones to place their Main Deck and Extra Deck. For Side Deck, player can place it an anywhere else.
[{Monster|monsters}] Zones: Where [{monsters|monsters}] are placed and [{battling|gameplay/battle-mechanics}].
[{Spell|spells}] & [{Trap|traps}] Zones: Where [{spells|spells}], [{traps|traps}] are placed and activated.
Pendulum Zones: The leftmost and rightmost [{Spell|spells}] & [{Trap|traps}] are also Pendulum Zones which used for placing [{Pendulum Monsters|monsters/pendulum-monsters}].
Field Zone: The zone used for placing [{Field Spell|spells/field-spells}].
Graveyard Zone (GY): The zone of used, destroyed or discarded cards.

Extra Monster Zones: Two player share 2 Extra Monster Zones together, although Main Monster Zones can also hold monsters from Extra Deck, but for [{Link Monsters|monsters/link-monsters}], those must be placed in Extra Monster Zones.

Each player start with 8000 LP (Life Points). Whoever can reduce opponent's LP to 0 (by [{battling|gameplay/battle-mechanics}], or effects...) wins the Duel, if both players' LP become 0, it will be treated as a draw.
A player's turn will include the following phases:
• Draw Phase: The turn player draw 1 cards from their [{Main Deck|basic/decks}].
• Standby Phase: A transitional phase between the Draw Phase and Main Phase 1.
• Main Phase 1: The turn player can summon [{monster|monsters}], activate or set [{spells|spells}], [{traps|traps}],...

• [{Battle|gameplay/battle-mechanics}] Phase: [{Battle|gameplay/battle-mechanics}] Phase: During this phase, turn player's monsters can attack and [{battle|gameplay/battle-mechanics}] with your opponent's monsters. Unlike other phases which player must enter, player can choose to skip the [{Battle|gameplay/battle-mechanics}] Phase.
• Main Phase 2: The same as Main Phase 1. If player skipped Battle Phase, the Main Phase 2 won't happen, of course...
• End Phase: The turn ends.
There are 4 types of summoning in Yu-gi-oh:
• Normal Summon: Place [{monster|monsters}] from hand to Main Monster Zones vertically and face-up.
• Set: Place [{monster|monsters}] from hand to Main Monster Zones horizontally and face-down.
• Flip Summon: When a [{monster|monsters}] is already Set, player can flip it up (place it vertically face-up in the same zone). But, a [{monster|monsters}] cannot be flipped in the turn it was Set.

• Special Summon: A type of summon which requires a special method or under specific conditions (can be placed either vertically or horizontally, face-up or face-down, by default, special summoned [{monsters|monsters}] must be face-up).
Notice:
Player can only Normal Summon or Set 1 monster once per turn, but can Flip Summon as many as possible if there is enough Set monsters.
There no limit for the times of Special Summon.
First, let's learn about Battle Position - it is the way that [{monsters|monsters}] was placed in the field:
• Attack Position: A [{monster|monsters}] is in Attack Position if it is placed vertically and face-up.
• Face-up Defense Position: A [{monster|monsters}] is in Face-up Defense Position if it is placed horizontally and face-up.
• Face-down Defense Position: [{Monsters|monsters}] that was Set.
Of course, a [{monster|monsters}] can't attack unless it is in Attack Position. When a [{monster|monsters}] attack another [{monster|monsters}]. There can be 3 situation:

• If both are in Attack Position: Which [{monster|monsters}] with lower ATK will be destroyed (and sent to [{GY|basic/playmat}]). The owner also lose LP equal to the ATK difference. If 2 [{monsters|monsters}] have the same ATK, both will be destroyed and players take no damage.

• If attacked [{monster}] is in face-up Defense Position: If attacking [{monster}]'s ATK is less than attacked [{monster}]'s DEF, it won't be destroyed, but the owner still lose LP equal to difference. If attacked [{monster}]'s DEF less than attacking [{monster}]'s ATK, it will be destroyed, but the owner won't lose any LP.
● If attacked [{monster|monsters}] is in face-down Defense Position: It must first be changed to face-up Defense Position, the rules will be apllied like the same above.
Notice:
A monster can only attack once per turn. While opponent control no monster, it can attack them directly and make them take damage equal to its ATK.
To reduce opponent's LP to 0, beside [{battling|gameplay/battle-mechanics}], there are some ways to do that:
• Using [{Spells|spells}] and [{Traps|traps}]: Some [{spells|spells}] and [{traps|traps}] have effect to deal damage directly to opponent.
• By [{monster's effects|monsters/effect-monsters}]: Some [{monsters|monsters}] also have effects to deal damage to opponent.
• Special Victory: Some card have special effects that can make player win when they meet its certain conditions.
A normal Monster Card will include:
• Card Name
• Attribute - There are 7 attributes:

• Level (1 - 12): For monster that is Level 4 or lower, you can [{Normal Summon|gameplay/summoning}] or [{Set|gameplay/summoning}] it without Tributing (remove other monsters from field) but for Level 5 / 6 monsters, you need Tributing 1 monster you control to [{Normal Summon|gameplay/summoning}]/[{Set|gameplay/summoning}] it (also called Tribute Summon). For Level 7 or higher monsters, you need tributing 2.
• Monster Image
• Monster Type
• Description (or Effect)
• ATK and DEF
Notice:
By default, tributed [{monsters|monsters}] will be sent to [{GY|basic/playmat}].
Normal Monster is monster card with no effects and can be Normal Summon, which mean its description doesn't affect to the gameplay. Normal Monster Card frame is yellow colored, like this one:
Notice:
Not every monster that has no effects is Normal Monster. It must have the word "Normal" in its type, if not, it will be called "non-[{Effect Monster|monsters/effect-monsters}]".
Effect monster is monster that has special abilites (effects). Effect Monster Card frame is brown colored.

This card's description says it couldnot be destroyed by [{battle|gameplay/battle-mechanics}] with monster that has 1900 or more ATK. Which mean if this card attacks (or is attacked by) a monster with 1900+ ATK, it won't be destroyed, but the owner still take the [{battle damage|gameplay/battle-mechanics}].
Notice:

A [{Ritual|monsters/ritual-monsters}] / [{Fusion|monsters/fusion-monsters}] / [{Synchro|monsters/synchro-monsters}] / [{Xyz|monsters/xyz-monsters}] / [{Link|monsters/link-monsters}] monster can also be an Effect monster.

Ritual monster is monster that can be [{Special Summon|gameplay/summoning}] (from hand) by using [{Ritual Spell|spells/ritual-spells}] and remove monsters (from field and/or hand]) whose total Level equal or exceed to the Level of Ritual monster. Of course, this method of summoning is called "Ritual Summon". Ritual Monster Card frame is light-blue colored.

To Ritual Summon, the player must activate [{Ritual Spell|spells/ritual-spells}] first, then sent the monsters (called "materials") from field and/or hand to the [{GY|basic/playmat}] (by default), then placed the Ritual Monster from hand to the field.
Notice:
Ritual Monster Card is inside the [{Main Deck|basic/decks}], which mean player has to draw it before can summon it.
If a monster is on the field, it must be face-up before being used as material. If a monster is on the hand, it must be revealed before being used as material.

Fusion monster is type of monster can be [{Special Summoned|gameplay/summoning}] (Fusion Summoned) from [{Extra Deck|basic/decks}] by using a [{spell|spells}] card called "{[Polymerization|24094653]}" (or "[{Fusion|search:fusion}]"), then remove its set of materials which list in the card description from field and/or hand. Fusion Monster Card frame is violet colored.

Look at this card description, it require 3 "Blue-Eyes White Dragon", which mean the player must send 3 copies "Blue-Eyes White Dragon" from field and/or hand to [{GY|basic/playmat}] (by default) after activating the "Polymerization".
Notice:
If a monster is on the field, it must be face-up before being used as material. If a monster is on the hand, it must be revealed before being used as material.

Synchro monster can be Special Summoned (Synchro Summoned) from Extra Deck to the field by remove monsters from the field whose total Level is exactly equal to the Level of Synchro monster. But, Synchro Summon require an unique type of monster called "Tuner". Synchro Monster Card frame is white colored while Tuner is just sub-type of monster and doesn't has its own frame color.

To Synchro Summon, the player just need to send all materials to [{GY|basic/playmat}] (by default), then place the Synchro monster to the field. Like the card above, the player need exactly 1 Tuner monster and 1 or more non-Tuner monsters.
Notice:
All monsters must be face-up before being used as materials.
Unlike other types of monsters, Xyz monster doesn't have the Level, instead, it has Rank. Beside the black-colored card frame, its stars is also placed in reversed position.
To Xyz Summon, the player need to stack monsters whose Level is equal to the Rank of Xyz monster, then place Xyz monster over them. Like the card above, the player will need 2 Level 4 monsters.
Xyz Effect Monster often requires sending its materials (detach materials) to GY to activate its effect

Like this card, it has 2 effects. First effect allow its to detach 1 materials to negate an attack from opponent's monsters while second effect will send it to GY if it is targeted for an attack while having no materials.
Notice:
Because of having no Levels, Xyz Monsters are immune to {[card effect that depends on monster's Level|85742772]}.

All monsters must be face-up before being used as materials. After Xyz Summon, they will no longer be not treated "are on the field". Also when they are detached, it won't be treated as "leave the field".
If a Xyz Monster leaves the field, all materials will be sent to GY, but like above, it won't be treated as "leave the field".

Pendulum monster is a very unique type of monster. It look like a combination of [{Spell|spells}] and [{Monster|monsters}]. The upper half of Pendulum Monster Card frame is green colored (like a [{spell|spells}]) while the lower half is colored like the type of [{monsters|monsters}].

Pendulum monsters will be placed in [{Extra Deck|basic/decks}] or Main Deck depends on its type of monster. For example, if it was [{Fusion|monsters/fusion-monsters}] / [{Synchro|monsters/synchro-monsters}] / [{Xyz|monsters/xyz-monsters}], it will be inside the [{Extra Deck|basic/decks}], if it was [{Normal|monsters/normal-monsters}] or [{Ritual|monsters/ritual-monsters}], it will be inside the [{Main Deck|basic/decks}].
A Pendulum monster can be used as a [{spell|spells}] or [{monster|monsters}] depends on where it is placed:
• As a [{Spell|spells}]: By placing Pendulum monster in a [{Pendulum Zone|basic/playmat}], it will treated as activating a [{spell|spells}] and also it will be treated as a [{spell|spells}].

If we look at the card, we can see that Pendulum Monster Cards have an additional description called "Pendulum Effect". While being placed in [{Pendulum Zones|basic/playmat}], the player can only use those effect of the card.
• As a Monster: The player still can Normal Summon / Set / Flip or Special Summon a Pendulum Monster like a monster. In that case, Pendulum Effect cannot be used.

All Pendulum Monsters has a special mechanics: If it would be sent from field to [{GY|basic/playmat}], it is placed face-up on top of the Extra Deck instead (but if it was sent from hand or [{Deck|basic/decks}], it still goes to [{GY|basic/playmat}]).
For examply: If we tribute a pendulum monster to summon another monster, that pendulum monsters will go to Extra Deck.
• Pendulum Summon:

To Pendulum Summon, first, the player need to have 2 Pendulum monsters in [{Pendulum Zones|basic/playmat}]. Then, look at the "Pendulum Scale" on the card (the blue and red crystal) of both cards. If both Pendulum Scales are different (like 1 and 8). it will create a Pendulum Scale Range.

Now, the player can special summon any number of monsters from hand and/or any number of face-up Pendulum monsters in Extra Deck whose Level are in Pendulum Scale Range but not equal to the lowest and highest values which means if Pendulum Scale Range is 1 - 8, the player can summon monsters from Level 2 - 7.
Notice:
If there is an effect that makes cards {[go to other places instead of GY|11448373]}, it will overwrite the mechanics of pendulum monsters.
A monster doesn't need to be a pendulum monster to be Pendulum Summoned.
For Xyz Pendulum Monsters, cause they [{don't have the Level|monsters/xyz-monsters}], they cannot be Pendulum Summoned by normal ways.
All monsters summoned from hand must be placed in [{Main Monster Zone|basic/playmat}] while all monsters summoned from Extra Deck must be placed in [{Extra Monster Zone|basic/playmat}].
Although the player has 2 [{Extra Monster Zone|basic/playmat}], but one of them can be used (for each player).

Link Monster can be easily Link Summoned by remove monsters from field (like [{Synchro Monster|monsters/synchro-monsters}]) but it needs to be placed in [{Extra Monster Zone|basic/playmat}]. Link Monster Card frame is dark-blue colored.

Like [{Xyz Monster|monsters/xyz-monsters}], Link Monster doesn't have the Level and moreover, it doesn't have the stars. Instead, it has 8 arrows around the card image, some will be red colored and called "Link Rating".
Link Monster's DEF will be replaced by "Link-n" when n is equal to its Link Rating. Therefore, a Link Monster cannot be placed in [{Defense Position|gameplay/battle-mechanics}].

To Link Summon, the player will need to remove a nummber of monsters equal to the Link Rating of Link Monsters. Like the card above, it has Link-3 and the card description says "2+ Effect Monsters" which means player need to 3 materials and atleast 2 of them must be Effect monsters.

Link Monsters also have the special mechanics: If a Link-n monster is used for Link Summon, it can act like n monster(s) or just 1 monster. For example, if you has 2 Link-2 monsters, you can Link Summon a Link-4 / Link-3 or another Link-2 Monster.
But, if the Link-4 monster description says "3+ monsters", it means the player still need atleast 3 actual monsters, so the player cannot just use 2 Link-2 monsters.

There is one more mechanic of Link monsters, any [{Main Monster Zones|basic/playmat}] that the Link arrows point to can be treated as [{Extra Monster Zone|basic/playmat}] for other Link monsters or [{Pendulum monster that were Special Summoned from Extra Deck|monsters/pendulum-monsters}] and only for that purpose.

If 2 Link Monster point to each other, that is called "co-link". If the player can make a series of co-link that point to the second [{Extra Monster Zone|basic/playmat}], they can take over that zone, like the one below:
Notice:

Like [{Xyz Monsters|monsters/xyz-monsters}], Link Monsters are immune to {[card effect that depends on monster's Level|44947065]}. Beside, Link Monsters are also immune to card effect that depends on monster's DEF or changes the [{Battle Position|gameplay/battle-mechanics}].

Spell Card have special effect(s) and need to be activated by placed it (from hand) to [{Spell & Trap Zones|basic/playmat}], spell card can bring to the player some advantage or create some disadvantages to the opponent. A Spell Card frame is green colored. A Spell Card will include:
• Card Name
• Spell Icon

• Spell Symbol (Type) - There're 6 types of spell: Normal, Equip, [{Ritual|monsters/ritual-monsters}], Continuous, [{Field|basic/playmat}] and Quick-Play. But Normal Spell Cards don't have the symbol.
• Spell Image
• Description (Spell Effects)
Notice:
Although [{Pendulum Monsters in Pendulum Zones|monsters/pendulum-monsters}] is treated as spells, they don't belong to any types above.
